title: Illuminated Tales: Decoding Stories in Indian Paintings
description: The program offered an engaging exploration of storytelling through Indian paintings, showcasing how art has long served as a powerful medium for narrating cultural and spiritual traditions. Scholars and participants delved into the unique Chitrakathi style from Paithan, celebrated for its bold lines, vibrant colors, and strong narrative focus. The session also highlighted the exquisite Ragamala painting series, where intricate imagery beautifully visualizes classical Indian musical modes.

title: An Indian Port City on the Arabian Peninsula
subtitle: Talk on Aden and Indian Labor
description: The lecture examined the rise of Aden as a global port city and the pivotal contributions of Indian laborers and entrepreneurs, recruited from Bombay and the Konkan coast, in its 19th-century growth. Using Bombay Presidency archives, the speaker traced the lives of Parsis, Bohras, Khojas, Menons, and other Indian communities, alongside Yemeni Muslims and Jews, to reveal the diverse social fabric and colonial contradictions that shaped Aden.

title: Crossing the Indian Ocean
description: The conference explored the rich seafaring and shipbuilding traditions of India's west coast, bringing together scholars, naval experts, and historians through a series of panel discussions. The sessions highlighted maritime traditions, indigenous navigation knowledge, and intercoastal engagements. These interdisciplinary dialogues on maritime networks, seafaring practices, and historical memory added valuable insights to the broader discourse on the Indian Maritime Knowledge System.

title: Sailing the Monsoons
subtitle: Darshak Itihas Nidhi, Vadnagar
description: The conference mapped the entanglements of seafaring traditions of the western Indian Ocean and the Indian Peninsula with the broader economic, technological, and knowledge circulations of the Indian Ocean world. Scholars discussed the evolution of shipbuilding techniques, navigational practices, and entrepreneurial frameworks, while also interrogating the contemporary relevance of these maritime traditions. Together, the sessions highlighted how these enduring practices continue to shape our understanding of the oceans and their role in global history.
